help.speed_rpm: The motor speed you want, in revolutions per minute. The controller tries to reach this value; the measured motor speed is shown separately.
help.ramp_s: How long the target takes to rise from zero to the chosen speed. For example, 0.5 means the target rises over half a virtual second.
help.load_before: The twisting resistance on the shaft before the load changes. A larger value makes the motor work harder.
help.load_after: The twisting resistance after the selected load-change time. Compare it with the initial load to make a harder or easier test.
help.step_s: The moment when the shaft load changes. A value of 2 means the load changes two virtual seconds after the run starts. This is NOT the calculation interval.
help.duration: How many virtual seconds to calculate. The opening run lasts 5 seconds. This is experiment time, not the time your computer needs to finish.
help.record_s: How often the run saves a row of results. A value of 0.001 saves one row every millisecond. The solver calculates between these saved rows.
help.Vb: The battery source voltage feeding the drive. This model does not calculate how full the battery is.
help.Rfeed: Resistance between the battery source and DC link. Current through it causes a voltage drop.
help.Idis: The maximum current the battery source may supply to the DC link.
help.Ichg: The maximum current the source may accept back from the link. This setting does not add a vehicle regenerative-braking experiment.
help.Cdc: The capacitor on the DC link. It temporarily stores electrical energy and helps smooth the inverter supply.
help.Rs: Resistance in each motor winding. It contributes to electrical losses.
help.Ld: Inductance on the motor d axis, which describes one direction of current in the rotating motor reference frame.
help.Lq: Inductance on the motor q axis. q-axis current is the main torque-producing current in this experiment.
help.psi: The strength of the permanent-magnet flux used in the motor equations.
help.pp: Number of north-south magnet pairs. Electrical angle turns this many times for one mechanical shaft turn.
help.J: How difficult it is to speed up or slow down the shaft. A larger inertia gives a slower mechanical response.
help.B: A friction term that grows with shaft speed. It makes the motor need extra torque.
help.gear: Motor turns per wheel turn. At a ratio of 8, eight motor turns give one wheel turn. This is a simple kinematic conversion.
help.rw: Wheel radius used to turn wheel rotation into an equivalent speed. No road motion or tyre slip is calculated.
help.switching: Averaged mode uses smooth bridge duties. Switched PWM applies the individual gate commands and needs much smaller calculation intervals.
help.fpwm: How many PWM switching cycles occur each second. This is electrical switching frequency, not animation speed.
help.mmax: The allowed modulation size. It limits how much voltage the controller can request from the inverter.
help.Imax: Limit on the torque-producing q-axis current request.
help.fci: How quickly the current controller is tuned to react. Higher is faster, but must remain compatible with the fixed solver interval.
help.fcs: How quickly the speed controller is tuned to react. Use small, justified changes when studying response.
help.zeta: The speed controller damping setting. It affects how smoothly the motor settles after a change.
help.Vac: The independent AC source RMS voltage for the rectifier experiment. It is not the drive battery voltage.
help.fac: How many AC cycles the rectifier source produces each second.
help.Rload: The independent rectifier load resistance. A smaller value asks for more load current.
help.Cf: The rectifier filter capacitor, which helps smooth the pulsating DC voltage.
help.Rsource: Resistance in the independent rectifier source path.
help.Vd: Voltage lost across each conducting diode in the rectifier bridge.
help.buckVin: The DC input voltage for this independent converter. It is separate from the motor drive source.
help.buckD: The fraction of each switching cycle commanded on. 0.75 means 75%. This converter uses averaged equations.
help.buckL: The converter inductor stores energy in its magnetic field and affects current change.
help.buckC: The output capacitor stores energy and helps smooth the output voltage.
help.buckR: The output load resistance. A smaller resistance draws more current at the same voltage.
help.buckrL: Resistance in the inductor. It represents a loss and changes the steady output.
help.buckStart: Empty startup begins with no stored inductor/capacitor energy. Steady state begins at the calculated equilibrium.
help.boostVin: The DC input voltage for this independent converter. It is separate from the motor drive source.
help.boostD: The fraction of each switching cycle commanded on. 0.75 means 75%. This converter uses averaged equations.
help.boostL: The converter inductor stores energy in its magnetic field and affects current change.
help.boostC: The output capacitor stores energy and helps smooth the output voltage.
help.boostR: The output load resistance. A smaller resistance draws more current at the same voltage.
help.boostrL: Resistance in the inductor. It represents a loss and changes the steady output.
help.boostStart: Empty startup begins with no stored inductor/capacitor energy. Steady state begins at the calculated equilibrium.

legends.Reference: The target value the controller is trying to follow.
legends.Motor: The calculated motor response. In torque charts this is produced motor torque; in speed charts it is actual speed.
legends.Load: The external twisting resistance on the motor shaft, or resistive load current in a converter chart.
legends.DC link: Voltage on the capacitor feeding the inverter.
legends.Supply into link: Electrical power entering the DC link from the source.
legends.Inverter AC: Electrical power at the ideal inverter AC output.
legends.Electromagnetic: Power converted between electrical and rotating motor states.
legends.Shaft load: Mechanical power absorbed by the imposed shaft load.
legends.Phase A: Calculated value in motor phase A.
legends.Phase B: Calculated value in motor phase B.
legends.Phase C: Calculated value in motor phase C.
legends.Carrier: The triangular comparison signal used to form PWM gate commands.
legends.q reference: The torque-producing current requested by the controller.
legends.q current: Calculated torque-producing current in the rotating reference frame.
legends.d current: Calculated current along the magnet-flux reference axis.
legends.Ideal reference: Lossless voltage reference; losses and transients can make output differ.
legends.AC source: The independent alternating voltage entering the rectifier.
legends.Full-wave bridge: The rectified voltage before the output capacitor smooths it.
legends.Filtered DC: Voltage after the rectifier filter capacitor.
legends.Diode charging: Current charging the filter capacitor through the diode bridge.
legends.Duty A: The requested on-fraction for phase A. 0 means off and 1 means fully on.
legends.Upper A: Ideal upper gate command for phase A: 1 on, 0 off. Paired upper/lower commands are complementary, without dead time.
legends.Lower A: Ideal lower gate command for phase A: 1 on, 0 off. Paired upper/lower commands are complementary, without dead time.
legends.Duty B: The requested on-fraction for phase B. 0 means off and 1 means fully on.
legends.Upper B: Ideal upper gate command for phase B: 1 on, 0 off. Paired upper/lower commands are complementary, without dead time.
legends.Lower B: Ideal lower gate command for phase B: 1 on, 0 off. Paired upper/lower commands are complementary, without dead time.
legends.Duty C: The requested on-fraction for phase C. 0 means off and 1 means fully on.
legends.Upper C: Ideal upper gate command for phase C: 1 on, 0 off. Paired upper/lower commands are complementary, without dead time.
legends.Lower C: Ideal lower gate command for phase C: 1 on, 0 off. Paired upper/lower commands are complementary, without dead time.

lessons: Find your way around

Left: choose an experiment and set the inputs. Right: inspect calculated results, playback, the drivetrain and graphs. The opening baseline calculates automatically. Change a setting and select Calculate experiment to replace the results. Invalid settings retain the previous completed run.
Your first drive experiment

Keep the baseline preset: target 1500 rpm, initial load 10 N m, final load 20 N m, load change at 2 s. After calculation is ready, Play results moves through the stored response; Pause holds the selected instant. Drag Simulation time to inspect any point. At 5 s, motor speed should be very close to 1500 rpm. The controller supplies extra torque after the 2 s load change.
Three different meanings of time

Load change time is WHEN the external load changes: 2 means two virtual seconds after the start. The solver calculation interval is HOW OFTEN equations are updated: averaged mode uses 0.00002 s (20 microseconds), so 50,000 steps cover one virtual second. Recording interval is HOW OFTEN a row is saved: default 0.001 s (one millisecond), giving 5001 rows from 0 to 5 s inclusive. Playback speed only changes how quickly you view those stored results. It does not change calculations.
Read the drivetrain

Battery source feeds the DC-link capacitor, then the inverter sends three-phase power to the permanent-magnet synchronous motor (PMSM). The motor turns a shaft, gear reduction and wheels. The 3D cutaway is generic teaching geometry. Rotor and wheel angles follow the selected calculated shaft angle, with wheel angle divided by the gear ratio. Reduced motion holds the rotating illustration still while readouts and graphs remain usable. No vehicle mass, tyre slip, road grade, distance, battery state of charge or thermal behaviour is calculated.
Read graphs and legends

The vertical scale names the unit and the horizontal scale is virtual seconds. The moving dashed cursor marks the selected instant; cards and the drive view follow it. Solid, dashed and dotted traces distinguish signals alongside colour. Hover, focus or tap an i button by a legend for its meaning. Reference is the requested value; Motor is the calculated response. Compare speed error, response after a load change, overshoot and settling rather than looking at one number alone.
Try and verify one change

Save the baseline CSV first. Choose the changed preset (1000 rpm, lower supply) and wait for completion. Inspect the final speed and compare the time response. Keep other inputs fixed when testing one parameter. Default end speed is about 1500 rpm and DC-link voltage about 298.9 V. Source power, inverter power and shaft power need not match during transients because energy is stored and losses are present.
Understand phases and PWM

Choose the switched PWM preset, then the Phase and PWM waveforms tab. Inspect the final 2 or 20 milliseconds. Three phase currents, phase voltages, phase duties, triangular carrier and all six gate commands are available at solver resolution. In averaged mode, gate traces are illustrative comparisons; in switched mode, they are applied to the bridge. Ideal paired switches have no dead time. Fast rotation and switching may appear to strobe; slow playback or pause to inspect samples.
Independent converter experiments

Buck reduces DC voltage; boost increases DC voltage; the rectifier changes AC into filtered DC. These experiments have separate sources and resistive loads. They are not attached to the motor drivetrain and are not a battery charger. Their inputs are grouped under advanced settings. Defaults settle near 300 V for buck and 400 V for boost. The lossy steady-state preset starts near 292.683 V and 382.979 V respectively.
Export and verify evidence

Recorded CSV covers the run at the selected recording interval. Fine waveform CSV covers the final 20 ms at the solver interval. Both preserve all 51 named columns. The baseline exports 5001 recorded samples plus the header. The switched preset exports 1201 recorded and 10001 fine samples plus headers. Coarse recording can miss switching peaks; use fine data for electrical waveform analysis. Exports are local learning evidence, not a hardware measurement.
Advanced solver and model boundaries

The preserved reference engine has 13 states integrated with fixed-step fourth-order Runge-Kutta. Averaged mode uses 20 microseconds. Switched mode uses the smaller of 2 microseconds and 1/(50 × PWM frequency). Validation rejects settings that exceed the browser step budget, produce unsuitable recording intervals or are too stiff for this fixed solver. Do not try to fix a rejected run by changing the playback rate.
Reference evidence

The supplied Edward programmer guide, implementation handover and portable executable provide the model specification. The preserved numerical suite contains 32 checks and 170 independent embedded MATLAB checkpoints across three scenarios. Original SLX and complete native binary traces were not supplied in this workspace, so the historical comparison of 1,100,003 samples has not been repeated. The 3D assembly improves presentation and does not establish manufacturer geometry, OEM calibration or additional physical validation.
